Re-estimate the temporal triggering kernel from EM responsibility weights

Source: R/trigger_reestimate.R
trigger_reestimate_temporal.Rd

Generalizes the original script's Loop-1 temporal triggering re-estimation: bins triggering-pair offsets into a weighted histogram (edge-corrected by trigger_edge_correction()'s output), smooths with ker.smooth.conv(), and re-normalizes – returning a "semihawkes_trigger_temporal" object, a drop-in replacement for trigger_temporal_init()'s output (same base grid, refreshed basevalue/fun).

Usage

trigger_reestimate_temporal(
  events,
  pairs,
  weights,
  edge_correction,
  temporal_trigger,
  bandwidth = 5
)

Arguments

events

A semihawkes_events object.

pairs

A pair index from trigger_pairs().

weights

Responsibility weights from trigger_pair_weights() (same length/order as pairs).

edge_correction

A semihawkes_trigger_edge_correction object from trigger_edge_correction().

temporal_trigger

The current semihawkes_trigger_temporal object (only its base grid is reused; basevalue/fun are replaced).

bandwidth

Gaussian smoothing bandwidth passed to ker.smooth.conv(); default 5 (matches the original script).

Value

A "semihawkes_trigger_temporal" object.

Examples

# \donttest{
# A quick fit to one year of the bundled simulated data: a coarse grid, a
# coarse triggering-kernel grid and two EM iterations keep it to a few
# seconds. Real analyses need finer settings and more iterations.
cache_dir <- tempfile("spHawkes_marks_")
fit <- fit_semihawkes(
  sim_events, sim_region,
  date_col  = "date",
  end_date  = "2022-01-01",
  cell_size = 1000,
  cache_dir = cache_dir,
  trigger_spatial_args = list(x_range = 2000, x_step = 250),
  trigger_window_dist  = 2000,
  n_iter  = 2,
  verbose = FALSE,
  seed    = 1
)
#> The modelled study period ends on 2021-12-29, the day after the last event. `end_date` (2022-01-01) is used only to select events and to label outputs.
pairs <- trigger_pairs(fit$events, window_days = 90, window_dist = 2000)
w <- trigger_pair_weights(fit$events, pairs, fit$A, fit$lambda_at_events,
                          fit$temporal_trigger, fit$spatial_trigger)
ec <- trigger_edge_correction(fit$events, fit$temporal_trigger,
                              fit$spatial_trigger, cache_dir)
g_new <- trigger_reestimate_temporal(fit$events, pairs, w, ec,
                                     fit$temporal_trigger)
plot(g_new$base, g_new$basevalue, type = "l", xlim = c(0, 30),
     xlab = "Days since event", ylab = "Density")

# }
